claims.statement: The reference applies across FPT, GHEC and GHES; GHEC managed-user names are controlled by the enterprise IdP administrator and members cannot rename themselves.

GHES LDAP or SSO users require local administrator rename according to the reference. This conflicts with DOCS-USERNAMERENAME-2 allowing LDAP self-change and differs from DOCS-USERNAMECHANGE-1's built-in-only introduction; authority remains unresolved.

In FPT/GHEC the repository retirement reusable permanently retires an old owner/repository pair for public repositories containing a Marketplace-listed action, more than 100 clones, or more than 100 Actions uses in the preceding week. Retired pairs cannot be recreated; these thresholds are not universal retention policy.

The package reusable says packages and container images move to the new namespace and dependent projects may break. In FPT/GHEC public container images with more than 5,000 downloads have their former full name permanently retired; this is a narrower condition than all packages.

Existing repository web links continue working after rename but may take minutes; command-line pushes to old remote URLs continue. This reference does not eliminate the separately recorded same-name redirect takeover risk or recommendation to update remotes.
Old username mentions and gist links cannot receive redirects. Repository redirect behavior must not be generalized to every identity reference.

Previously verified commits signed with the old GitHub-provided noreply address lose Verified status after rename. The described verification checks exact committer/tagger email against GPG identities and verified account linkage; retained contribution attribution is a separate property.

In FPT/GHEC numeric-ID noreply format ID+USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com preserves account attribution/contribution graph association after rename; older username-only forms do not. This exception does not guarantee preserved signature verification.

Linked username policy, managed identity and authentication documentation remain separate review work. No namespace is renamed, threshold measured on a target, rights granted or native behavior verified.
